title: Playwright for AI Applications
description: Title slide introducing Lecture 4: Playwright for AI Applications, with a four-stage roadmap covering Dynamic Content, Streaming, Resilient Selectors, and Scaling Up.

title: Learning Objectives
description: What You'll Be Able To Do: four concrete outcomes covering asserting on dynamic AI content, testing streaming responses, writing resilient selectors, and testing loading/error states.

title: Why Traditional E2E Tests Break
description: Problem statement: why traditional E2E tests fail on AI-powered UIs — hardcoded text assertions, streaming timing races, and selectors tied to volatile generated content.

title: What's Different About Testing an AI UI
description: Three layers of an AI UI test: the request, the streaming/incremental render, and the final rendered output — presented as a layered stack diagram.

title: The Playwright AI Toolkit
description: Toolkit overview introducing the three techniques covered in this lecture: dynamic content assertions, streaming response tests, and resilient selector patterns.

title: Setting Up Test Fixtures for AI Apps
description: Practical setup concerns for AI app tests: seeding conversation state, mocking auth, and resetting rate limit counters between tests.

title: Worked Example: Asserting on Dynamic AI Content
description: Worked example showing how to write Playwright assertions that pass on valid AI responses without hardcoding exact generated text.

title: Patterns for Asserting on Generated Content
description: A comparison card grid of assertion patterns for AI-generated content: regex/structure checks, normalized snapshot testing, semantic assertions, and the exact-text anti-pattern.

title: Testing Streaming Responses
description: Concept slide explaining strategies for asserting on incrementally-delivered streaming responses: waiting for completion signals, testing partial UI state, and avoiding fixed waits.

title: Waiting for the Right Signal
description: Deep dive comparing waitForResponse, waitForFunction/custom polling, and fixed sleep() — explaining why the first two are reliable and sleep() is not.

title: Worked Example: Testing a Streaming Response
description: Worked example of a Playwright test that synchronises with a streaming AI response using real completion signals rather than arbitrary timeouts.

title: Testing Cancelled and Interrupted Streams
description: Covering user-cancelled generation and network drops mid-stream as explicit test cases, including what to assert after each interruption scenario.

title: Writing Selectors That Survive AI Output Changes
description: Concept slide on preferring role and testid-based selectors over text-content selectors, and structuring the DOM so tests target stable containers rather than volatile generated text.

title: Naming Conventions for data-testid
description: Practical guidance on naming and placing stable data-testid attributes in an AI-generated UI tree, covering role+entity naming, stable containers, stream state attributes, and index anti-patterns.

title: Worked Example: Brittle vs. Resilient Selectors
description: Worked example contrasting a brittle text-based selector that breaks on AI output changes with a resilient role/testid selector that survives any phrasing.

title: Accessibility as a Resilience Strategy
description: Using getByRole and getByLabel (a11y-driven selectors) as a bonus source of resilient, semantic selectors — with a priority ranking of selector strategies.

title: Testing Loading & Error States
description: Concept slide covering the AI response lifecycle: loading/typing indicators, timeout handling, and graceful error UI assertions for each state.

title: Simulating Rate Limits and Failures
description: Testing how the UI behaves under simulated 429 and 5xx responses from the AI backend, and verifying retry/backoff UI using page.route() interception.

title: Taming Flakiness at Scale
description: Slide on running AI Playwright tests reliably in CI: smart retry strategy, mocking the model layer for deterministic runs, and keeping a real-model smoke suite.

title: Mocking the Model Layer
description: Intercepting network calls to return deterministic fixture responses for fast, non-flaky CI runs — with a real-model vs. mocked comparison table.

title: Visual Regression on Dynamic UIs
description: Snapshot testing strategy that masks dynamic AI text regions while still catching real layout regressions — stable vs. unstable snapshot target classification.

title: Running Many AI Tests in Parallel Safely
description: Test isolation concerns specific to AI apps: shared rate limits, conversation state bleed, and isolating fixtures per worker — with an isolation checklist.

title: A CI Pipeline for AI E2E Tests
description: Two-track CI pipeline: fast mocked suite on every PR plus a scheduled real-model smoke suite — covering sharding, retry policy, and artefact retention.

title: Debugging Flaky AI Tests
description: Using Playwright's trace viewer and video capture to reproduce and diagnose non-deterministic failures in AI test suites.

title: Case Study: A Chat Support Widget
description: A short narrative case study wiring dynamic-content assertions, streaming waits, and resilient selectors together in a realistic five-step chat widget test.

title: Check Your Understanding
description: Three knowledge-check questions with answers testing core lecture concepts: wait strategies, parallel isolation, and resilient selector choices.

title: Tools You Can Use Today
description: A six-card recap grid mapping Playwright ecosystem capabilities — network interception, trace viewer, visual comparisons, sharding, accessibility selectors, retry/flake detection — to the techniques covered.

title: Testing Isn't Just About Correctness
description: A teaser slide framing prompt-injection and security-focused E2E testing as a related but separate topic, with a correctness vs. security comparison table pointing to a future lecture.

title: Common Pitfalls to Avoid
description: Three Playwright AI testing pitfalls: asserting on exact generated text, using sleep() instead of real signals, and never testing the failure path.

title: Key Takeaways
description: Three-pillar summary: dynamic content assertions, streaming tests, and resilient selectors — the three techniques every Playwright AI test suite needs.
